title: AI Product Videos & Photos for Beauty Brands | Aidreamcapes
description: Make AI product videos and photos for beauty brands: texture close-ups, routine clips, and kit shots from one photo of your bottle or jar. Try it today.
h1: AI Product Videos and Photos for Beauty Brands, From Swatch to Shelf
lead: Show the texture, the packaging, and where your product fits in a morning or evening routine, starting from one photo of your bottle, jar, or tube.
intro: Beauty shoppers can't touch, smell, or swatch anything through a screen, so your images have to do that work for them. They want to see how a cream looks when it's scooped, whether a serum is clear or tinted, and how big the bottle is in a hand. Clean packshots still matter, because they carry your product page and your marketplace listing.

Pair a photo of your serum or balm with a sentence about the setting you picture: a marble vanity in soft morning light, toner pressed onto a cotton pad, a travel kit laid out on a folded towel. Videos can run 6, 10, or 15 seconds, vertical for TikTok and Reels or square for feeds. Every photo comes out square by default, a good fit for listings and carousel posts.

ideas.d: A slow 6-second clip of cream being scooped or serum falling from a dropper shows consistency better than a written description. Name the color and thickness in your request so the texture looks like your actual formula.
Put your product into a quick morning or night routine: cap off, a pump into the palm, back on the shelf. Vertical 9:16 fits Stories, Reels, and TikTok without awkward cropping.
If you sell a set, show every piece together in one square image so shoppers know exactly what arrives. Lay all the items out before you take your upload photo.
Place a moisturizer on a bathroom shelf, a lipstick in a makeup bag, or a sunscreen in a beach tote. Scenes like these give your gallery a sense of everyday use beyond the white background.

faq.q: Can I make before-and-after videos for a skincare product?
faq.a: We'd steer away from it for skin results. A generated face isn't evidence of what your product does, and a visible change in skin reads as a promise. Show application, texture, and packaging instead, and leave claims about results out of your request and your ad copy.

faq.q: Will the video match my exact foundation or lipstick shade?
faq.a: Color comes from your photo and your wording, so shoot in daylight and name the shade plainly, like "warm beige liquid" or "brick red matte." If the tone still drifts, generate another version; the credit cost is shown before each one.

faq.q: Can I add my price or a promo code to the image?
faq.a: Type prices, promo codes, and product names on afterward in Canva or CapCut. Lettering made by AI can come out misspelled, so keep the image clean and add the words yourself.

faq.q: What kind of product photo should I upload for skincare?
faq.a: A straight-on shot with the label toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands or clutter in the frame. Glossy tubes and clear glass pick up glare, so shoot beside a window rather than using flash.
